narrative:
The model estimates a 59% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the company has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

The decision is driven mainly by three aspects of your profile. First, your overall work experience of only 1–5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward staying. Most employees the model expects to remain also have relatively short careers, so the system sees this as a stabilizing element. However, the other two key factors pushed more strongly in the opposite direction. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important reason the model leaned toward leaving; having external opportunities often signals that someone is considering or being pulled elsewhere. Third, your relatively short time in this specific organization (also 1–5 years) added further weight toward departure, as longer tenure in the current role is more common among those the model predicts will stay.

Taken together, the combination of limited total experience, active external opportunities, and short current tenure outweighed the stabilizing signals and led to the 59% probability of leaving.

You and the organization should consider two practical next steps: exploring whether those external offers can be matched internally, and discussing a clear timeline for gaining more responsibility and recognition here so the model would view you as more likely to stay in the future.
